subject: domestic dogs, rabies and wildlife
title: What If Every Dog on Earth Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every dog on Earth vanished tonight? One deadly disease would almost disappear with them.
Overnight, roughly eight hundred million dogs are gone. About three in four aren't pets but free-roaming dogs.
Within years, rabies would nearly vanish. Dogs cause up to ninety-nine percent of human cases.
Wildlife would gain too. Dogs threaten at least one hundred eighty-eight endangered species and helped drive eleven to extinction.
But millions of people would lose guide dogs, sniffer dogs and herding dogs, all at once.
We'd lose our oldest animal partner. The earliest known dogs lived beside Ice Age hunters fifteen thousand years ago.

description:
What if every dog vanished? There are an estimated 700 to 900 million dogs, about three quarters of them free-ranging, and the WHO says dogs cause up to 99% of human rabies cases.
A 2017 global review found dogs have contributed to 11 vertebrate extinctions and threaten at least 188 threatened species; ancient DNA puts the earliest known dogs at about 15,800 years ago.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Which animal would you miss most if it vanished overnight? Tell us your what-if.
